title: Generative Modeling with Flux Matching
author: arxiv.org
summary: Flux Matching is a new method for generative modeling that learns a family of vector fields to generate data distributions, extending to noise-annealed settings like diffusion models. It allows choosing vector fields with useful properties, such as faster sampling, unlike traditional score matching methods. Although powerful, Flux Matching is more computationally expensive and is best used when the structure of the generative vector field matters.
